Tactus LLM Guidance (Canonical)

This file is intended for AI assistants and automated tooling. It describes the
canonical concepts and patterns for writing correct, modern Tactus code.

Key idea:
- Models produce signals.
- Procedures make decisions.
- Agents do open-ended work.

================================================================================
MODEL PRIMITIVE
================================================================================

One-sentence definition:
A Model is Tactus's stateless prediction interface: typed input -> typed output,
with a registry-backed lifecycle for training, versioning, and evaluation.

Model vs Agent:
- Use a Model for classification/extraction/scoring ("input in, output out").
- Use an Agent for multi-turn reasoning and tool use.

Canonical runtime call pattern (always use this):

  local m = Model("imdb_nb")
  local result = m({text = input.text})
  local out = result.output or result

Why "out = result.output or result" matters:
- Some backends return a raw output table.
- Others return a wrapper with an "output" field.

Single-file design (Option A):
Training configuration lives inside the same Model block under "training".
Training writes to the registry; runtime reads from the registry.

  Model "imdb_nb" {
    type = "registry",
    name = "imdb_nb",
    version = "latest",
    input = { text = "string" },
    output = { label = "string", confidence = "float" },
    training = { data = {...}, candidates = {...} }
  }

CLI (canonical):
- Train:
    tactus train file.tac --model imdb_nb
- Evaluate (registry-backed):
    tactus models evaluate file.tac --model imdb_nb

Registry tags (canonical):
- latest
- candidate/<candidate_name>

Dependencies (do not assume heavy ML deps in the core install):
- Core runtime:
    pip install tactus
- sklearn training (e.g. naive bayes):
    pip install "tactus[ml]"
- Hugging Face training:
    pip install "tactus[hf]"

GPU control (Hugging Face training):
Hugging Face Trainer uses GPU automatically when available.
To force CPU, pass through TrainingArguments:

  hyperparameters = {
    model = "distilbert-base-uncased",
    training_args = { no_cuda = true }
  }

Testing story (canonical):
Specs should test procedure logic, not model quality.
Use Mocks for deterministic CI:

  Mocks {
    imdb_nb = {
      conditional = {
        {when = {text = "Great movie."}, returns = {label = "positive", confidence = 0.91}},
        {when = {text = "Bad movie."}, returns = {label = "negative", confidence = 0.88}}
      }
    }
  }

Do NOT:
- Do not invent a "Model.predict()" DSL method. Models are called like functions.
- Do not assume "pip install tactus" includes datasets/transformers/torch.
- Do not treat evaluation as retraining (evaluation scores a registry-backed model).

================================================================================
AGENT PRIMITIVE (SHORT NOTE)
================================================================================

Agents are stateful multi-turn runtimes. They can use tools and iterate.
Procedures should keep deterministic control flow in code and use agents for the
non-deterministic steps that benefit from intelligence.
